  Fix first
    1. F1   sshd is open to any source on 22/tcp                                                  +5
    2. F2   Forwarded port 8022/tcp is open to any source                                         +1

  Findings

  HIGH     F1   sshd is open to any source on 22/tcp                                              -5
                IPv4: accepted by filter/INPUT rule #4.
                filter/INPUT #4:  -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
                fix  If the clients are known, accept only their addresses. If SSH must stay open to
                     any source, limit new connections for each source: the limit counts every
                     source by itself, so one client cannot lock out the others, and it does not
                     touch established sessions.
                     Replace the rule with one for the known clients:
                       iptables -R INPUT 4 -s <trusted-cidr> -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
                     Or drop the connections of a source that opens more than 10 a minute, in front
                     of the rule:
                       iptables -I INPUT 4 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh4 -j DROP

  MEDIUM   F2   Forwarded port 8022/tcp is open to any source (possible)                          -1
                nat/PREROUTING translates these ports to another host, and filter/FORWARD accepts
                them from any source; the rules of filter/INPUT do not apply: IPv4 8022/tcp to
                192.168.122.50:22 (via eth0).
                nat/PREROUTING #1:  -i eth0 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 8022 -j DNAT --to-destination 192.168.122.50:22
                fix  The port is translated by nat/PREROUTING rule #1 and then passes
                     filter/FORWARD, not filter/INPUT. If only known clients need it, add their
                     sources (-s <trusted-cidr>) to that rule or to the FORWARD rule that accepts
                     the traffic. In FORWARD the packet has the translated address and port; match
                     the original port with '-m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8022 --ctdir ORIGINAL'.

  Open to any source
    tcp  22 sshd

  Translated to other hosts
    8022/tcp → 192.168.122.50:22: any source, possible
    These ports are translated in nat/PREROUTING and pass filter/FORWARD, not filter/INPUT.
